name: gradio-rag-thin
description: A start-GREEN Gradio chatbot scaffold for retrieval-augmented generation that ships ONLY primitives (a real pgvector vector store, an offline embedder, and a real model-completion call) plus a fixed corpus — the RAG logic itself (retrieval, relevance gating, grounding, citation) is written by the build, NOT pre-supplied. This is the THIN counterpart to gradio-rag-llm: same rails, no solution code, used to measure how much of a RAG PoC the harness can assemble on its own.
interface: core.generate_reply(message: str, history: list | None = None) -> str
knowledge:
This PoC answers a user's question grounded in a FIXED private corpus, and an unrelated question (outside the corpus) must get a no-match reply rather than a made-up answer. The scaffold ships PRIMITIVES to compose — it does NOT ship the retrieval/grounding/citation logic (that is what the build must write). The primitives are: `search(query, k)` → the k corpus documents nearest the query by semantic similarity, as `[{id, title, content, distance}]` (smaller distance = closer; it ALWAYS returns up to k and does NOT decide relevance — the build does); `llm(prompt, system=...)` → a real model completion (the wording VARIES run to run); and `CORPUS` (the fixed docs as `{id, title, content}` — the PoC may NOT add facts not in it). Phrase every criterion around a topic the corpus actually covers; a criterion the fixed corpus cannot satisfy is unbuildable.
Because the model's prose is NON-deterministic, criteria/tests must assert what the build CONTROLS and can check deterministically — NEVER an exact sentence the model must produce. Make each criterion DISCRIMINATING: contrast an in-corpus question (the behaviour should fire) against an out-of-corpus one (it should not), so a fixed canned reply cannot pass, and check that an in-corpus answer is actually grounded in / verifiable against the corpus document it used rather than invented.
